headline: Persian Gulf Oil Exports Surpass Pre-War Highs
summary: Oil exports in the Persian Gulf have exceeded pre-war levels, with more than 24 million barrels flowing daily despite a record number of Iranian attacks, according to analysts.
why: The Persian Gulf is a vital maritime chokepoint for global petroleum transit. Export volumes directly influence international crude oil supply dynamics and tanker shipping economics.

impacts.name: Brent Crude
impacts.why: Higher export volumes and resilient supply flows ease concerns over regional physical crude shortages.

why_moved: Recovery in export volume despite geopolitical conflict reduced supply disruption risk premiums in international petroleum markets.
